model.name: Change Request
model.purpose: Represent a formal, identifiable proposal to alter a controlled subject (configuration item, document, requirement set, service or process), together with its classification, justification, impact and risk assessment, routing to a competent change authority, and the disposition recorded against it.
model.scope_statement: This model defines the change request as a record: what is proposed, against which baseline, why, with what assessed impact, to which authority it is routed, and what disposition and effectivity it carries. It is format-neutral: JSON, RDF/Turtle, Markdown, relational and document stores are projections. It owns the request-side view only. It does not own the requirement records it traces to (WM-REC-006), the decision that resolves it (WM-KNW-010), the configuration items and baselines it targets, the work that implements it, or the audit-trail store that evidences handling.
in_scope: Identity, origination and provenance of the change request record itself
Statement of the proposed change as a delta from an approved baseline, and the set of affected items, documents, interfaces and sites
Classification of the request: change type (standard, normal, emergency), instrument kind (permanent change, deviation, waiver), priority, urgency and claimed severity
Justification, drivers and outgoing traceability references to requirements, defects, nonconformances and audit findings
Impact, effort, risk, safety, security, privacy and regulatory-notification assessment content produced for this request
Routing metadata: which change authority was selected, on which criteria values, and whether the package is admissible
Disposition outcome recorded on the request, the binding to the authoritative decision record, and attached conditions and effectivity terms
Request state model, permitted transitions, supersession, withdrawal and reopening
Proposed implementation approach, backout intent, test intent and proposed window, as proposal content only
Closure recording, realisation references, variance between proposed and realised change, and evidence references
Retention class, legal-hold flags and confidentiality classification declared on the request record
Status accounting extracts and population measures over change request records
out_of_scope: Requirement definition, requirement text, requirement versioning, requirement baselining and requirement lifecycle (owned by WM-REC-006)
Decision semantics: deliberation, alternatives evaluation, decision rationale, decider mandate and decision-record lifecycle (owned by WM-KNW-010)
Definition of change-authority mandates, delegation limits and decision rights; this model records only which authority was routed to
Execution of the change: work orders, tasks, builds, change sets, releases, deployments and rollback execution
Configuration item master data, baseline composition and the issuing of new baselines
The audit-trail store and any evaluation, enforcement or attestation engine; access decisions are evaluated externally
Incident, problem, defect and nonconformance triage and lifecycle
Enterprise risk register lifecycle; only assessment outputs attached to this request are held here
Contractual change orders, variation pricing and contract amendment execution
Execution of retention schedules, disposal and destruction certification
Person, role and organisation master data and identity proofing

boundary_notes.distinction: The request carries typed trace references (affects, implements, tracks) with a version binding, mirroring OSLC CM link semantics. Requirement content, state and re-baselining are read-only from here; a withdrawn requirement invalidates the local link, not the requirement.

The request records the disposition value, the disposition timestamp and a reference to the decision record. Rationale, options considered, deliberation and the authority's mandate live in the decision model. Reversal is expressed here as a new state bound to a new decision reference, never as an edit of a prior outcome.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Change implementation, work-order and release model
boundary_notes.distinction: Everything before disposition is proposal content; everything after is execution. The request holds a proposed window, approach outline and backout intent; scheduling, task state, deployment and rollback execution belong to the executing model, referenced through a tracked change-set or work-record link.

Affected items and the target baseline are referenced by identifier and version. This model never asserts item structure or releases a new baseline; configuration identification and baseline release are separate configuration management activities.

A deviation authorises departure before manufacture or delivery, and a waiver accepts an already-nonconforming item; neither alters approved configuration documentation, whereas a change proposal does. The model classifies the instrument kind and holds expiry and quantity limits, but does not merge the two concepts.
An originating defect is a trigger reference (OSLC affectedByDefect). Defect triage, reproduction and closure remain with the originating model; closing a request does not close the defect.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Audit trail and status accounting store
boundary_notes.distinction: Status accounting extracts produced here are read-only projections over request records at a stated as-at instant. Immutable event logging, tamper evidence and audit-record retention are owned by the adopting Dimension's audit store; a reference to it grants no audit-trail semantics.

The request declares a retention class, a legal-hold flag and a tombstone shape. Schedule authorship, disposal execution and destruction evidence are owned by the adopting Dimension's records policy and, where regulated, by the applicable quality management system regulation.
A pre-authorised standard change is still a change request with an authority pre-bound by a change model; a service request that consumes an existing, unchanged service capability is not in scope.

sources.title: OSLC Change Management Version 3.0. Part 1: Specification
sources.relevance: Normative resource model for a ChangeRequest: resource types (ChangeRequest, ChangeNotice, Defect, Enhancement, ReviewTask, Task), state handling, relationship properties and representation requirements. Primary anchor for identity, relationships and interoperability.

sources.title: OSLC Change Management Version 3.0. Part 2: Vocabulary
sources.relevance: Field-level vocabulary: approved, authorizer, closed, closeDate, fixed, inProgress, reviewed, verified, state, status, priority, severity, parent, relatedChangeRequest, affectsRequirement, implementsRequirement, tracksRequirement, affectedByDefect, tracksChangeSet. Grounds candidate data elements and alignment mappings.

sources.title: ISO 10007:2017 Quality management — Guidelines for configuration management
sources.relevance: Defines the configuration management process as configuration management planning, configuration identification, change control, configuration status accounting and configuration audit. Establishes change control and status accounting as the process context for a change request. Guidance, not certifiable.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 20000-1:2018 Information technology — Service management — Part 1: Service management system requirements
sources.relevance: Management-system requirements covering configuration, change, release and deployment within a service management system. Supports admissibility, routing and closure obligations expressed as requirements rather than practice.

sources.title: NIST Special Publication 800-53 Revision 5, Update 1: Security and Privacy Controls for Information Systems and Organizations
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Catalogue containing the Configuration Management (CM) control family, the reference point for documented change proposals, impact analysis and change approval expectations in security-regulated adopting Dimensions.

sources.title: NIST Special Publication 800-128: Guide for Security-Focused Configuration Management of Information Systems
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
sources.relevance: Security-focused configuration management guidance covering configuration change control, security impact analysis and monitoring. Grounds the security-impact assessment finding and the separation of assessment from enforcement.

sources.title: ECSS-M-ST-40C Rev.1 — Configuration and information management
sources.organization: European Cooperation for Space Standardization (ECSS) / European Space Agency
sources.relevance: Requirements for configuration and information management across customer and supplier levels in space projects, including change and information control against baselines. Independent (non-US, non-IT) confirmation that change requests are baseline-relative and multi-party.

sources.title: NPR 7123.1D — NASA Systems Engineering Processes and Requirements (Updated w/ Change 2)
sources.relevance: Directive establishing configuration management and technical assessment as common technical processes with defined products and reviews. Supports assessment provenance, status accounting and the distinction between technical assessment and decision analysis.

sources.title: RFC 3339 — Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Normative timestamp format: seconds are part of the grammar and time-offset is either 'Z' or a numeric +/-HH:MM offset; '-00:00' denotes a known UTC instant with unknown local offset. Governs every time value in this model.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Entity/Activity/Agent with wasAttributedTo, wasAssociatedWith, wasGeneratedBy, wasDerivedFrom, generatedAtTime and invalidatedAtTime. Alignment target for record-level provenance of requests and their assessments, keeping provenance format-neutral.

sources.title: Quality Management System Regulation (QMSR)
sources.version_or_date: Final rule published 2 February 2024 (89 FR 7496); effective 2 February 2026; incorporates ISO 13485:2016 by reference into 21 CFR part 820
sources.relevance: Worked example of a jurisdiction where controlled change, change records and retention obligations are legally binding and where the regulation delegates detail to an incorporated international standard. Grounds regulatory-notification and retention findings, and the regional-assumption caveats.

sources.title: Change enablement in ITIL 4 — Change Enablement in the Cloud (AWS Well-Architected)
sources.version_or_date: Accessed 29 August 2026; cites ITIL 4 Change Enablement Practice Guide (PeopleCert)
sources.relevance: Restates the ITIL 4 definition of a service change ('addition, modification, or removal of anything that could have a direct or indirect effect on services') and the purpose of change enablement (assess risk, authorise, manage the change schedule). Used because ITIL 4 itself is not openly published; treated as secondary evidence of common practice, not as a normative requirement.

sources.title: MIL-HDBK-61A(SE) Configuration Management Guidance
sources.organization: U.S. Department of Defense (Office of the Under Secretary of Defense, Systems Engineering); copy hosted by AcqNotes
sources.relevance: Used only for terminology discrimination between engineering change proposal, request for deviation and request for waiver, and for effectivity concepts (units, serials, lots). Cited as a mirrored copy, so treated as secondary; no process obligation is imported from it.

bundles.name: Request Identity and Change Subject
bundles.description: What a change request instance is, how it is identified and originated, and exactly which controlled subject, baseline and scope the proposal targets.
bundles.rationale: Change control begins with unambiguous identification of the proposal and of the items and baseline it would alter; without both, the request cannot be routed, assessed, traced or reported. ISO 10007 places change control after configuration identification for this reason, and OSLC gives the ChangeRequest a resource identity independent of any store.

layers.name: Identity and Origination
layers.description: The identifiers that make a request addressable and the provenance of its raising.

data_elements.description: Authoritative master-system identifier of the change request.

data_elements.name: Request IRI

Materialising an identity document would create a second thing to keep synchronised with the record it names, and no cited source requires an identity artifact distinct from the request record itself.

data_elements.name: Intake channel
data_elements.description: Coded route through which the request entered the register.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Origination is captured as attribution and timestamp fields aligned to PROV-O agent and time properties. There is no separately governed submission document; producing one would duplicate fields already carried on the request and would fork provenance across two objects.

layers.name: Change Subject and Proposed Delta
layers.description: The controlled items and baseline targeted by the request and the substance of what would change.

findings.name: Affected items, baseline and scope boundary
findings.description: The configuration items, documents, interfaces and services the change would alter, the baseline the delta is expressed against, the sites or environments in scope, and explicit exclusions.

questions.text: Which configuration items, documents, interfaces or services would the proposed change alter?
Against which baseline or approved configuration is the proposed delta expressed?
answer_data: Date or event at which the baseline was frozen

questions.text: Which sites, fleets, environments or organisational units fall inside the proposed scope?
What is explicitly excluded from the proposed scope, and why?
answer_data: Items deliberately left on the current baseline

data_elements.name: Affected item references
data_elements.description: References to configuration items, documents, interfaces or services in scope, each with a version binding.

data_elements.name: Baseline reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the approved baseline against which the delta is stated.

data_elements.name: Scope site or environment references
data_elements.description: Sites, environments, fleets or jurisdictions to which the proposal applies.

data_elements.name: Scope exclusion statement
data_elements.description: Explicit statement of what the proposal does not cover.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Scope is a set of typed references plus short exclusion statements. Item structure, versions and baseline composition are owned by the configuration item and baseline model; copying them into a local artifact would create a stale duplicate of another model's authoritative content.

findings.name: Proposed change delta
findings.description: The substance of the proposal expressed as a difference from the current approved state, its content classification, and the feasibility evidence submitted with it.

questions.text: What exactly is proposed to change, expressed as a delta from the current approved state?
Which content classification applies to the delta: addition, modification, removal or reversion?
How is the delta represented so that it stays readable independently of any storage format?
What evidence accompanies the request that the described delta is technically achievable as stated?
answer_data: References to analyses, prototypes or prior art

data_elements.name: As-is description
data_elements.description: Description of the current approved state of the affected subject.

data_elements.name: To-be description
data_elements.description: Description of the proposed state after the change.

data_elements.name: Delta kind
data_elements.description: Coded classification of the change content as addition, modification, removal or reversion.

data_elements.name: Feasibility note
data_elements.description: Statement and supporting references on the technical achievability of the delta.

artifacts.name: Change proposal statement
artifacts.description: The governed statement of the proposed change: as-is state, to-be state, per-item delta, content classification and stated assumptions. It is the object a change authority reads and the object a disposition attaches to.
media_or_form: narrative text (Markdown, HTML or PDF rendering)
attached engineering representation (drawing, model or diff)
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent request identifier plus a monotonically increasing revision label; each revision is retained and never overwritten, so a disposition always names the exact revision it dispositioned.

bundles.name: Classification and Justification
bundles.description: How the request is typed and prioritised, why it is being made, and what it traces back to.
bundles.rationale: Change type determines the route, the required content and the authority; justification and traceability are what allow the request to be judged and later audited. ITIL 4 distinguishes standard, normal and emergency changes; configuration management practice distinguishes configuration-changing proposals from deviations and waivers; OSLC provides the trace link vocabulary.

layers.name: Classification and Typing
layers.description: The type, instrument kind, governing change model and relative importance assigned to the request.

findings.name: Change type, instrument kind and governing change model
findings.description: Assignment of standard, normal or emergency type; discrimination between a permanent configuration change and a time- or quantity-limited deviation or waiver; the change model or template that governs handling; and any regulated category that forces a stricter route.

questions.text: Which change type applies to this request, and what evidence supports that assignment?
answer_data: Criteria values that produced the assignment

questions.text: Is this a permanent configuration change, or a time- or quantity-limited departure that leaves the approved configuration documentation unchanged?
answer_data: Limit basis where the instrument is limited
Reason the documentation is or is not altered

questions.text: Which change model, template or pre-authorised procedure governs the handling of this request?
answer_data: Deviations from the model and their justification

questions.text: Which regulated, safety-related or contractual category does the change fall into, and does that category force a stricter route?
answer_data: Route escalation triggered by the category

data_elements.name: Change type
data_elements.description: Coded change type such as standard, normal or emergency.

data_elements.name: Instrument kind
data_elements.description: Whether the request is a configuration-changing proposal, a deviation or a waiver.

data_elements.name: Change model reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the change model, template or pre-authorised procedure applied.

data_elements.name: Regulated category
data_elements.description: Coded regulatory, safety or contractual category attaching to the change.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Classification is a small set of coded values plus the criteria values that produced them. The code lists themselves are governed by external classifier registries of the adopting Dimension and are referenced, not reproduced here as an artifact.

findings.name: Priority, urgency and claimed severity
findings.description: The relative importance assigned to the request, the urgency imposed by a need date or exposure window, the severity of consequence claimed if the change is not made, and how these are recomputed as the request changes.

questions.text: What priority value is assigned to the request, on which defined scale, and by whom?
What consequence and severity are claimed if the request is not implemented?
By which date or event must the request be dispositioned for it to remain useful?
How are priority and urgency recomputed when the request is superseded or its scope changes?
answer_data: Prior values with their validity intervals

data_elements.name: Priority
data_elements.description: Assigned relative importance of the request on a declared scale.

data_elements.name: Severity
data_elements.description: Claimed severity of consequence if the request is not implemented.

data_elements.name: Needed-by instant
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant or referenced event by which disposition is required.

data_elements.name: Priority scale reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the scale definition that gives the priority and severity codes their meaning.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Priority, urgency and severity are coded scalar values with a scale reference and a revaluation history. They are queried and sorted as fields; a document form would obstruct the population-level ranking these values exist to support.

layers.name: Justification and Traceability
layers.description: The stated reason for the change and the outgoing trace references that make it auditable.

findings.name: Drivers, justification and claimed benefit
findings.description: The business, technical, safety, security or regulatory driver behind the request, the consequence of inaction, any obligation that compels the change, and the benefit claimed with its measurement basis.

questions.text: What driver justifies the request, and into which driver category does it fall?
What would be the consequence of taking no action, and over what horizon?
Which obligation, audit observation or external mandate compels the change, if any?
What benefit or objective is claimed, and how would it be measured after implementation?

data_elements.name: Driver category
data_elements.description: Coded category of the driver, such as corrective, adaptive, regulatory, safety or security.

data_elements.name: Justification narrative
data_elements.description: Stated reason for the change in the submitter's own terms.

data_elements.name: Compelling obligation reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a mandate, audit finding or regulatory obligation that compels the change.

data_elements.name: Claimed benefit measure
data_elements.description: Benefit statement with an associated measure and target value.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Justification is narrative and reference content that belongs on the request so that it travels with every projection of it. Benefit realisation tracking after implementation belongs to the executing and benefits models, so no local artifact is warranted here.

findings.name: Requirement and origin traceability links
findings.description: Typed outgoing references from the request to requirements it affects, implements or tracks, and to the defect, nonconformance or finding that originated it, including version binding and behaviour when a target is withdrawn.

questions.text: Which requirements does the request affect, implement or track, and under which link type is each recorded?
answer_data: Direction and cardinality of each link

questions.text: Which originating defect, problem, nonconformance or audit finding does the request answer?
How is each outgoing trace reference pinned to a specific version of the target record?
answer_data: Resolution rule when the pin is unavailable

questions.text: What happens to the trace set when a referenced requirement is withdrawn or re-baselined by its owning model?
answer_data: Local link state after target withdrawal
Notification or review obligation raised locally

data_elements.name: Requirement trace link
data_elements.description: Typed reference to a requirement record with link type (affects, implements, tracks) and version pin.

data_elements.name: Origin record trace link
data_elements.description: Typed reference to the defect, nonconformance or finding that originated the request.

data_elements.name: Link resolution state
data_elements.description: Local state of each outgoing link: resolved, stale, unresolved or withdrawn-target.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Traceability here is purely a set of typed, version-pinned references held on the request. A local traceability matrix artifact would duplicate content owned by WM-REC-006 and by the originating defect model, and would go stale the moment either target changed.

bundles.name: Assessment and Authorization Routing
bundles.description: The assessment content produced for the request and the routing that places it in front of a competent change authority.
bundles.rationale: ISO 10007 and space and defence configuration management practice require impact evaluation before a change is approved; security-focused configuration management adds a security impact analysis. Routing selects who may decide but is not itself a decision — that separation is the central boundary of this model.

layers.name: Impact and Risk Assessment
layers.description: Technical, schedule, cost, risk, safety, security, privacy and regulatory assessment content attached to the request.

findings.name: Technical, interface and verification impact
findings.description: Which interfaces, verification results and qualification statuses the change would invalidate, what re-verification it obliges, which dependent items inherit impact, and who produced the assessment and when.

questions.text: Which functional and physical interfaces, verification results or qualification statuses would be invalidated by the change?
What re-verification, re-qualification or retesting would the change oblige?
Which dependent items or downstream deliverables inherit the impact of the change?
answer_data: Whether the dependent needs its own request

questions.text: Who performed the technical impact assessment, on which revision of the proposal, and when?

data_elements.name: Impacted interface references
data_elements.description: References to interfaces, verification records and qualification statuses affected by the change.

data_elements.name: Re-verification obligation
data_elements.description: Activity that must be repeated to restore verification standing after the change.

data_elements.name: Assessor reference
data_elements.description: Party that produced the technical impact assessment.

data_elements.name: Assessed proposal revision
data_elements.description: Revision label of the change proposal statement to which the assessment applies.

artifacts.name: Impact assessment record
artifacts.description: Governed record of the technical impact evaluation for one revision of the proposal: affected interfaces, invalidated verification, dependent items, re-verification obligations, assessor attribution and assessment timestamps.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent request identifier plus the assessed proposal revision label and an assessment sequence number, so a re-assessment after a proposal revision is a new record rather than an edit.

findings.name: Schedule, cost and resource impact
findings.description: Effort, cost and schedule implications with stated confidence, the resources and long-lead items the change would consume, the commitments it would affect, and how estimate revisions are recorded.

questions.text: What effort, cost and schedule change does the proposal imply, and at what stated confidence?
answer_data: Effort, cost and duration estimates with units

questions.text: Which resources, skills, facilities or long-lead items would the change consume?
Which delivery, funding or contractual commitments would be affected by the change?
How are estimate revisions recorded as the request is re-assessed?

data_elements.name: Effort estimate
data_elements.description: Estimated implementation effort with unit and confidence.

data_elements.name: Cost estimate
data_elements.description: Estimated cost impact with currency and confidence.

data_elements.name: Schedule impact
data_elements.description: Estimated change in duration or milestone dates caused by the change.

data_elements.name: Affected commitment reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a delivery, funding or contractual commitment affected by the change.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Estimates are versioned quantitative fields with validity intervals; they are aggregated across the request population and compared against realised values. Holding them as a document would prevent that aggregation, and the authoritative cost and schedule baselines themselves live in the planning and finance models.

findings.name: Risk, safety, security, privacy and regulatory impact
findings.description: Assessed risk of implementing and of not implementing the change, the security impact analysis result, effects on safety functions and personal data processing, and whether external notification or prior approval is required.

questions.text: What is the assessed risk of implementing the change and, separately, of not implementing it?
What security impact analysis result applies, including effects on controls and authorisation boundaries?
Does the change affect safety functions, hazard controls or the processing of personal data?
answer_data: Safety function or hazard control references

questions.text: Does the change require notification to, or prior approval from, an external regulator, customer or certification body?

artifacts.name: Risk and security impact analysis
artifacts.description: Governed analysis attached to a proposal revision covering implementation and non-implementation risk, security impact on controls and authorisation boundaries, safety and privacy effects, and any external notification obligation identified.

layers.name: Authorization Routing
layers.description: Selection of the competent change authority and confirmation that the request package is admissible for consideration.

findings.name: Competent authority routing and package readiness
findings.description: Which change authority the request was routed to, on which criteria values, whether the package is admissible for consideration, and what fallback applies when the authority is unavailable. Records routing facts only; the authority's mandate and the act of deciding belong to the decision model.

questions.text: Which change authority was this request routed to as competent under the criteria applied?
Which routing criteria were applied, and what were their values at the moment of routing?
answer_data: Criteria names and values at routing time
Party or service that performed the routing

questions.text: Is the request package complete and admissible for consideration by that authority?
What escalation or fallback route applies when the routed authority is unavailable or declines competence?

data_elements.description: Reference to the change authority the request was placed before.

data_elements.name: Routing criteria snapshot
data_elements.description: Criteria names and values captured at the moment of routing.

data_elements.name: Admissibility verdict
data_elements.description: Whether the package was judged complete enough for consideration, with the missing-content list.

data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant at which the request was routed to the authority.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Routing produces facts about the request — which authority, which criteria values, whether admissible — not a governed document. Deliberately no artifact is declared here: an approval or review package artifact would drift toward owning decision content, which the relation to WM-KNW-010 reserves to the decision model.

bundles.name: Disposition and Request Lifecycle
bundles.description: The outcome carried by the request, the conditions and effectivity attached to it, and the states the request itself moves through over time.
bundles.rationale: The registry purpose names disposition explicitly, and configuration management requires that an approved change carry an effectivity so that implementers know which units, versions and dates it applies to. The request-side lifecycle is distinct from both the decision that resolved it and the work that implements it.

layers.name: Disposition and Effectivity
layers.description: The recorded outcome, its binding to the authoritative decision, and the conditions and effectivity that scope an approval.

findings.name: Disposition outcome and decision binding
findings.description: The outcome value carried by the request, the reference and version binding to the decision record that resolved it, the times at which disposition occurred and was recorded, and how reversal or reopening is represented without rewriting history.

questions.text: What disposition outcome does the request carry: approved, conditionally approved, rejected, deferred, withdrawn or superseded?
Which decision record authoritatively resolved the request, and how is that reference bound and versioned?
answer_data: Decision record reference and version pin

questions.text: When did the disposition occur, and when was it recorded against this request?
answer_data: Explanation where the interval is material

questions.text: How is a later reversal or reopening of a dispositioned request represented without rewriting the earlier outcome?
answer_data: Successor outcome entry with its own decision reference
Validity interval of the superseded outcome

data_elements.name: Disposition outcome
data_elements.description: Coded outcome recorded against the request.

data_elements.name: Decision record reference
data_elements.description: Version-pinned reference to the decision record in WM-KNW-010 that resolved the request.

data_elements.name: Dispositioned at
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 event time at which the disposition was made.

data_elements.name: Disposition recorded at

The governed document that carries rationale, options and the decider's mandate is the decision record owned by WM-KNW-010; declaring a local disposition artifact would reproduce that model's content and violate the reference boundary.

findings.description: Provisos attached to an approval, the point from which the approved change becomes effective, the population and locations it applies to, and the expiry or quantity limit of a deviation or waiver.

From which unit, serial, lot, version, date or event does the approved change become effective?
To which sites, fleets, environments or jurisdictions does the effectivity apply?
What is the expiry or quantity limit of a deviation or waiver, and what happens when it is reached?

data_elements.description: Proviso attached to an approval, with its verifier and satisfaction state.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Effectivity and conditions are structured field values that downstream execution and manufacturing systems must query mechanically (which serials, from which date, to which sites). layers.name: Request Lifecycle and Time

findings.description: The permitted states of a change request, the legal transitions between them, terminal states and reopening rules, entry preconditions, and control of concurrent editing.

Which states are terminal, and under what rules may a terminal request be reopened?
Which preconditions must hold before a request may leave assessment and enter routing?
How is concurrent editing of a request in a non-terminal state detected and controlled?

data_elements.name: State transition event

data_elements.name: Record version token
data_elements.description: Token used for optimistic concurrency control on the request record.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The state model is a vocabulary and a transition table expressed as configuration of the model, and the per-instance data is a current-state code plus a transition list. No governed document is produced, and the immutable event log that some adopters derive from transitions belongs to the audit store, not here.

findings.name: Temporal discipline and derived durations

data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant at which a modelled occurrence took place, with explicit seconds and offset.

data_elements.name: Observation or ingestion time

data_elements.name: Derived age
data_elements.description: Duration derived at read time from a declared timestamp pair and an as-at instant.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Temporal discipline is a set of field-level rules and stored instants, not a produced object. Externalising it as an artifact would separate the rule from the values it governs; the rules themselves are declared once in the model's service layers.

bundles.name: Proposed Implementation Envelope and Closure
bundles.description: What the request proposes about how the change would be carried out, and what it records when the change has been realised.
bundles.rationale: ITIL 4 change enablement and common practice require an implementation approach, a backout intent and a proposed window before authorisation, while configuration management requires closure to be evidenced. Both are held here as proposal and closure facts, with execution owned by the implementing model.

layers.name: Proposed Implementation Envelope
layers.description: Approach, backout intent, test intent, proposed window and constraints, all as proposal content.

findings.name: Proposed approach, backout intent and test intent

questions.text: What implementation approach does the request propose, at the level of detail needed to judge it?
What backout, remediation or rollback intent accompanies the proposal, and what condition triggers it?
answer_data: Maximum time to restore the prior state

questions.text: What test or validation intent is proposed to demonstrate the change performs as claimed?
Where does the proposal end and the executing work order or release plan begin?

data_elements.name: Implementation approach outline
data_elements.description: Proposed approach and major steps as submitted for judgement.

data_elements.name: Backout intent
data_elements.description: Proposed means of reverting, with trigger condition and restoration time.

data_elements.name: Test intent
data_elements.description: Proposed validation activity and acceptance criteria references.

data_elements.name: Execution record reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the work order, change set or release record that executes the change.

artifacts.name: Proposed implementation outline
artifacts.description: The proposal-stage description of how the change would be carried out, sufficient for an authority to judge feasibility and risk. It is superseded by, and never substitutes for, the executing model's implementation plan.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent request identifier plus the proposal revision label it accompanies; superseded outlines are retained so a disposition can be read against the outline that existed at the time.

artifacts.name: Backout and remediation outline
artifacts.description: The proposal-stage statement of how the prior state would be restored, including the trigger condition or decision point at which backout is invoked and the tolerated restoration time.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent request identifier plus the proposal revision label; retained alongside its outline so that the pair judged by the authority stays reconstructable.

findings.name: Proposed window, dependencies and disruption tolerance
findings.description: The implementation window proposed against calendars and freeze periods, the dependencies and blackout constraints that bound it, the maximum tolerated disruption implied, and the notification expected before the window opens.

questions.text: What implementation window is proposed, and against which calendar or freeze periods was it checked?
Which dependencies, predecessor changes or blackout constraints bound the proposed window?
What is the maximum service disruption the proposal implies, and to whom?
Which stakeholders are expected to be notified before the proposed window opens, and how far ahead?

data_elements.name: Proposed implementation window
data_elements.description: Proposed start and end instants for carrying out the change, in RFC 3339 form.

data_elements.name: Window dependency reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a predecessor change, blackout period or constraint bounding the window.

data_elements.name: Expected disruption
data_elements.description: Expected outage or degradation duration implied by the proposal.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The proposed window is a pair of instants plus constraint references that must be machine-comparable against the change schedule owned by the executing model. The authoritative change schedule is not produced here, so no local artifact is justified.

layers.name: Closure and Evidence
layers.description: How a request is closed, what realisation and verification it references, and how supporting evidence is bound to it.

findings.name: Closure and realised-outcome referencing

questions.text: On what basis is a change request considered closed, and who may close it?
Which implementation, release or work records does the closed request reference as realisation evidence?

questions.text: Which post-implementation review or verification result is referenced, and which model owns it?

data_elements.name: Realisation reference

data_elements.name: Variance statement

data_elements.name: Closed at

artifacts.description: The record that terminates the request: closure criteria satisfied, close code, closing party, realisation references, variance statements and references to verification or post-implementation review owned elsewhere.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent request identifier alone, because a request has at most one closure record; a reopening produces a new request state and, on subsequent closure, a successor closure record linked to the prior one.

findings.name: Supporting evidence binding and integrity
findings.description: The documents, models, analyses and datasets attached to or referenced by the request, how their integrity is asserted, how broken references are detected, and which evidence carries restricted or personal data.

questions.text: Which supporting documents, models, analyses or datasets are attached to or referenced by the request?
How is the integrity and immutability of each referenced evidence item asserted?
Which evidence items are held externally, and how are broken or moved references detected?
Which evidence carries restricted, export-controlled or personal data requiring separate handling?

data_elements.description: Reference to a supporting document, model, analysis or dataset, with its role in the request.

data_elements.name: Evidence digest

data_elements.name: Evidence restriction classification
data_elements.description: Handling restriction applying to an evidence item, such as restricted, export-controlled or personal data.

artifacts.name: Evidence manifest
artifacts.description: The list binding a request to its supporting evidence: reference, role, contributing party, digest, last successful resolution and handling restriction per item.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent request identifier plus a manifest sequence number; a new manifest version is issued whenever evidence is added, replaced or found unresolvable, and prior versions are retained.

bundles.name: Relationships and Interoperability
bundles.description: How requests relate to one another, how references to other models are bound, and how the model maps to external vocabularies without overclaiming conformance.
bundles.rationale: OSLC Change Management defines parent, related, supersession-adjacent and cross-domain link properties, and requires machine-readable representations. Alignment claims must be recorded as mappings, since ISO 10007 is guidance and ITIL is not openly published.

layers.name: Request-to-Request and External Relationships
layers.description: Links between change requests and the binding rules for references leaving the model.

findings.name: Relationships between change requests
findings.description: Supersession, duplication, dependency and blocking links between requests, parent and child decomposition, detection of cycles and contradictions, and the effect of rejection or withdrawal on dependants.

questions.text: Which other change requests does this request supersede, duplicate, depend on or block?
How are parent and child decomposition relationships between requests expressed and constrained?
How are cycles, contradictory pairs and orphaned children detected and prevented?
What happens to dependent requests when this request is rejected or withdrawn?

data_elements.name: Related request reference
data_elements.description: Reference to another change request with a typed relationship.

data_elements.name: Parent request reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the parent request in a decomposition hierarchy.

data_elements.name: Supersession reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the request that supersedes, or is superseded by, this one.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Inter-request relationships are typed edges on the request record, consistent with the registry's typed-edge link default. A relationship document would add nothing beyond the edges themselves and would need to be regenerated on every graph change.

findings.name: External reference binding and resilience
findings.description: How references to records in other models are expressed so they remain resolvable, whether they are version-pinned or floating, which model owns lifecycle for each referenced record, and what is recorded when a target cannot be resolved.

questions.text: How is a reference to a record in another model expressed so that it stays resolvable across systems and projections?
answer_data: Target model identifier and record key

questions.text: Is a given reference pinned to a target version, or does it float to the target's current state?
Which referenced model owns lifecycle, evaluation and enforcement for each referenced record?
answer_data: Owning model identifier per reference class
Locally held attributes versus target-owned attributes
Prohibited local operations on the target

questions.text: What is recorded locally when a target model or record is unavailable at reference time?

data_elements.name: External reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a record in another model, carrying target model identifier, record key, pinning mode and link type.

data_elements.name: Reference resolution state
data_elements.description: State of an external reference: resolved, unresolved, stale or target-withdrawn, with the last successful resolution instant.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Reference binding is a field-level convention plus per-reference metadata carried on the request. The registries that make targets resolvable are external, and reproducing them locally as an artifact would create a competing and quickly stale directory.

layers.name: Interoperability and Standards Alignment
layers.description: Declared mappings to external change-management vocabularies, their conflicts, and the projection-neutrality contract.

findings.name: Standards alignment, conflicts and lossless projection
findings.description: Which external vocabularies the model claims mapping to and at what level, where mapped terms genuinely conflict, how neutrality across serialisations is preserved, and what minimal profile a projection must preserve to count as lossless.

questions.text: To which external change-management vocabularies does the model claim alignment, and at which level of strength?
answer_data: Alignment strength: mapping, partial or conformance

answer_data: Local resolution and the term left unmapped

answer_data: Constructs forbidden because they are storage-specific

answer_data: Mandatory field set for the profile

data_elements.description: Declared mapping to an external vocabulary with target version and claim strength.

data_elements.name: Term mapping
data_elements.description: Mapping between a local element and an external term, including unmapped and conflicting cases.

data_elements.name: Interchange profile
data_elements.description: Named minimal field set that a projection must preserve for lossless exchange.

artifacts.name: Alignment mapping table
artifacts.description: The governed table mapping this model's elements to external change-management vocabulary terms, recording claim strength, unmapped elements and known semantic conflicts. It is the evidence behind every alignment statement the model makes.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the model identifier plus the alignment target identifier and a mapping version number; a new version is issued whenever the model or the aligned vocabulary version changes.

bundles.name: Assurance, Access and Retention
bundles.description: Admissibility and quality control over the request population, status accounting, confidentiality classification, and retention and disposition of request records.
bundles.rationale: ISO 10007 makes configuration status accounting a first-class part of the configuration management process, and regulated regimes make records and their retention legally binding. Access classification and retention class are declared on the record; evaluation, enforcement and disposal execution sit with other models.

layers.name: Validation and Status Accounting
layers.description: Admissibility rules, duplicate and conflict detection, and reporting over the change request population.

findings.name: Admissibility, completeness and conflict detection
findings.description: Content mandatory by change type, the checks run at submission and their failure handling, detection and merging of duplicates, and detection of open requests that would alter the same item in contradictory ways.

questions.text: Which content is mandatory for a request to be admissible, and how does that vary by change type?
answer_data: Mandatory field set per change type

questions.text: Which automated checks run at submission, and what happens when one fails?
How are duplicate or near-duplicate requests detected, and how are they merged or linked?
How are two open requests that would alter the same item in contradictory ways detected?
answer_data: Overlap detection rule on affected items

data_elements.name: Mandatory content rule
data_elements.description: Rule declaring which content is mandatory for a given change type.

data_elements.name: Validation result
data_elements.description: Outcome of a submission check, with check identifier, verdict and timestamp.

data_elements.name: Duplicate link
data_elements.description: Link asserting that this request duplicates or is duplicated by another, with the surviving record indicated.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Validation produces verdicts and rule references attached to the request, and the rulesets themselves are model configuration rather than instance artifacts. Emitting a validation report artifact would duplicate the verdicts already carried and would tempt consumers to treat it as an audit record, which this model does not own.

findings.name: Status accounting and population measures
findings.description: The status accounting views that must be producible over the request population, the measures that characterise its health, the authoritative source behind each reported figure, and the distinction between live snapshots and as-at reconstructions.

questions.text: Which status accounting views of the change request population must be producible on demand?
Which measures characterise the health of the change request population, and how is each defined?
What is the authoritative source for each reported figure, and how is double counting avoided?
answer_data: Source field or record per figure
Exclusion rules for superseded or duplicate requests

questions.text: Which reported figures are live snapshots and which are as-at reconstructions of a past instant?
answer_data: Restatement policy when late data arrives

data_elements.name: Status view definition
data_elements.description: Definition of a status accounting view: filter, grouping and required fields.

data_elements.name: Population measure
data_elements.description: Defined measure over the request population, such as cycle time, emergency share or rejection rate.

data_elements.name: As-at instant
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 instant at which a reported figure is stated to hold.

artifacts.name: Status accounting extract
artifacts.description: A read-only projection over change request records at a stated as-at instant, giving the configuration status accounting view of proposed and dispositioned changes. It reports; it is not an audit record and carries no tamper-evidence guarantee.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the view definition identifier plus the as-at instant and an issue sequence number, so that a restated extract for the same instant is distinguishable from the original.

layers.name: Access Classification and Retention
layers.description: Confidentiality classification declared on request records, and the retention class, holds and tombstone shape applied at end of life.

findings.name: Confidentiality classification and need-to-know
findings.description: The handling classification carried by the request record, parts restricted below the record level, personal data present and its basis, and readability of rejected or withdrawn requests. Classification is declared here; evaluation and enforcement are external.

questions.text: What confidentiality or handling classification does the request record carry, and who assigned it?
Which parts of the request are restricted below the classification of the record as a whole?
Which personal data appears in a request, and on what basis is it held?
Who may read a request that has been rejected or withdrawn, and for how long?
answer_data: Permitted reader roles after terminal disposition
Model that evaluates the access decision

data_elements.name: Classification code
data_elements.description: Confidentiality or handling classification declared on the request record.

data_elements.name: Restricted element marker
data_elements.description: Marker identifying an element restricted below the record-level classification.

data_elements.name: Personal data category
data_elements.description: Category of personal data present in the request, with the basis for holding it.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Only classification labels and restriction markers are held on the record. Access policies, the evaluating engine and the resulting access log belong to the adopting Dimension's access control and audit models; declaring an access artifact here would imply ownership of evaluation and audit semantics that the model explicitly disclaims.

findings.name: Retention, holds and disposition of request records
findings.description: How long a request and its assessment content must be retained and under whose rule, what is deleted, redacted or preserved as a tombstone, which holds suspend disposal, and who executes disposal without this model owning the audit trail.

questions.text: How long must a change request and its assessment content be retained, and which rule sets that period?
answer_data: Trigger event that starts the clock

questions.text: What is deleted, what is redacted and what is preserved as a tombstone at the end of retention?
answer_data: Referential integrity guarantee for inbound links

questions.text: Which legal hold, investigation or dispute flag suspends disposal, and who may set or clear it?
answer_data: Party permitted to set and clear

questions.text: Who executes disposal, and how is the disposal evidenced given that this model does not own the audit trail?
answer_data: Evidence reference produced by that owner
Local record of the disposal outcome

data_elements.name: Retention class
data_elements.description: Declared retention class assigning the request to a schedule owned by the adopting Dimension.

data_elements.name: Legal hold flag
data_elements.description: Flag suspending disposal of the request pending legal, investigative or dispute action.

data_elements.name: Tombstone marker
data_elements.description: Marker recording that the request has been disposed of, retaining identifier, terminal state and disposal reference only.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Retention is expressed as a class code, a hold flag and a tombstone shape on the record. The schedule, the disposal action and the destruction certificate are produced and evidenced by the records management model of the adopting Dimension, so no artifact is created here.
